Christopher Columbus

Blockchain technology is like a shared digital notebook that everyone can see but no one can secretly edit. Instead of one central authority controlling the data, the information is spread out across many computers, which makes it very secure and transparent. Each page of this notebook, called a "block," holds a group of transactions. Once a page is filled and verified, it is locked in place using advanced math (cryptography) that ties it securely to the previous page. Because each page is linked to the one before it, changing any past record would require altering every single page that follows, which is practically impossible. This structure makes the system extremely resistant to fraud and tampering.
